history.title: Tax Cap Slider Gauge

style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a mechanical slider gauge on a warm oak desk surface. A graphite grey sliding block is pushed aggressively past a rigid bone white threshold marker. Three recognisable engineered parts: a track, a slider block, and a bolted limit line. One directional light from the top left casting long hard contact shadows. Clean physical arrangement, extreme asymmetry with the gauge pushed right, matte muted palette of graphite, bone white, and ochre. No text, no numbers, no embossed lettering, generous negative space.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random lettering, numbers, UI, symbols, watermarks, letters, typography
rationale: The news is structural and abstract: a flat amount of money being pushed past a rigid cap by an external force (exchange rates). A clay render of a mechanical threshold being overrun captures this without risking generated numbers or text on documents.
subject: a mechanical slider gauge with a block pushed past a limit line
core_thesis: Exchange rate fluctuations dictate whether a static foreign salary exceeds the fixed US dollar tax exclusion cap.
core_conflict: Fixed US dollar tax caps versus fluctuating foreign currency exchange rates.
composition: extreme asymmetry with the gauge pushed right
